report_name: Ransomware Attacks Surged 25% in a Year, Reaching 7,551 Victims

threat_actors.name: Qilin
threat_actors.description: Identified as the most prolific ransomware group in the Black Kite "2026 Ransomware Report", operating a Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) model and responsible for a significant number of the 7,551 publicly disclosed victims between April 2025 and March 2026.
threat_actors.goals: Financial extortion through data encryption and the threat of data leakage.

threat_actors.name: The Gentlemen
threat_actors.description: Identified as one of the top five most active ransomware groups in the Black Kite "2026 Ransomware Report", contributing to the 43.6% of attacks attributed to the top operators.
threat_actors.goals: Financial extortion through data encryption and the threat of data leakage.

attack_patterns.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack_patterns.description: Unpatched vulnerabilities in public-facing infrastructure, particularly VPNs and network edge devices, were cited as a primary initial access vector for ransomware attacks during the reporting period.

attack_patterns.name: Phishing
attack_patterns.description: Phishing remains a primary initial access vector for ransomware groups according to the report's analysis of attack trends.

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts
attack_patterns.description: The use of stolen credentials is a primary initial access vector for ransomware attacks.

attack_patterns.name: OS Credential Dumping
attack_patterns.description: Ransomware operators dump credentials, for example by accessing LSASS memory with tools like Mimikatz, to facilitate lateral movement within a victim network.

attack_patterns.name: Disable or Modify Tools
attack_patterns.description: As a precursor to encryption, ransomware operators attempt to disable or tamper with security software such as antivirus and EDR solutions.

attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: Encrypting victim data is the primary method of impact used by ransomware groups to extort payment.

attack_patterns.name: Inhibit System Recovery
attack_patterns.description: Ransomware operators delete volume shadow copies using tools like vssadmin.exe to prevent system recovery from local backups.

attack_patterns.name: Domain Account Discovery
attack_patterns.description: Ransomware operators use tools like AdFind.exe and native commands such as 'net group "Domain Admins"' to discover privileged accounts for lateral movement and privilege escalation.

attack_patterns.name: Domain Trust Discovery
attack_patterns.description: Ransomware operators execute discovery commands like 'nltest /dclist' to map out domain trust relationships for lateral movement planning.

attack_patterns.name: Clear Windows Event Logs
attack_patterns.description: Ransomware operators may use 'wevtutil.exe cl' to clear Windows Event Logs to hide their activity.

malware.name: Qilin
malware.description: A ransomware family used by the Qilin group, which was the most prolific ransomware operator between April 2025 and March 2026. The group uses a double extortion model, encrypting data and threatening to publish it on a leak site.

tools.name: AdFind
tools.description: Mentioned as a tool used by ransomware operators for Active Directory discovery and reconnaissance.

tools.name: Mimikatz
tools.description: Mentioned as a tool used by ransomware operators to access LSASS memory for credential dumping.

tools.name: vssadmin
tools.description: Mentioned as a tool used by ransomware operators to delete volume shadow copies to inhibit system recovery.

identities.name: Manufacturing Sector
identities.description: Identified as the most heavily victimized industry for ransomware attacks for the fourth consecutive year.

infrastructure.name: Ransomware Leak Sites
infrastructure.description: Data leak sites are a key component of the double extortion model used by ransomware groups, where stolen data is published to pressure victims into paying the ransom.

indicators.name: VSSAdmin Shadow Copy Deletion
indicators.pattern:
title: VSSAdmin Shadow Copy Deletion
id: 5b9f0a1e-3b2c-4d5e-8f6a-9b8c7d6e5f4a
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of vssadmin.exe to delete volume shadow copies, a common precursor to ransomware deployment.
references:
  - https://blackkite.com/reports/2026-ransomware-report
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-07-29
tags:
  - attack.t1490
  - attack.impact
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\vssadmin.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'delete'
      - 'shadows'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the use of vssadmin.exe to delete volume shadow copies, a common ransomware TTP mentioned as a hunting hint in the report.

indicators.name: Active Directory Discovery with Native Tools
indicators.pattern:
title: Active Directory Discovery with Native Tools
id: f9e8d7c6-b5a4-4987-6543-210fedcba987
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of native Windows tools like nltest and net for Active Directory discovery, often seen during ransomware operations.
references:
  - https://blackkite.com/reports/2026-ransomware-report
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-07-29
tags:
  - attack.t1482
  - attack.t1087.002
  - attack.discovery
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_nltest:
    Image|endswith: '\nltest.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/dclist'
  selection_net:
    Image|endswith: '\net.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'group'
      - '"Domain Admins"'
  condition: 1 of them
indicators.description: Detects the use of native Windows tools (nltest, net) for Active Directory discovery, as suggested in the report's hunting hints.
